An IED attack on a police vehicle in Karak District, resulted in the deaths of one policeman and wounding of six. An ex-commander of Ansar-ul-Islam who had made peace, was assassinated in Peshawar. Two insurgents were killed in a CTD operation in Katlang and a suspected TTP insurgent was killed in a joint CTD-FIA raid in Karachi. Police defused an IED targeting Garaj checkpost in Orakzai District. The vehicle of Miranshah AC was fired upon by insurgents in North Waziristan. Four civilians were injured in a quadcopter strike in the Splay Panra area of Toi Khulla tehsil.
On 1 September, two insurgents were killed in a joint operation in Lakki Marwat District, while one was killed in a failed attack on a security post in DI Khan District. Two children were injured in a drone strike in South Waziristan. An IED was neutralized in Karak District. Afghanistan announced a ban on Pakistani medications.
On 2 September, Pakistani forces killed 15 TTP insurgents infiltrating across the Pak-Afghan border in North Waziristan. Four TTP TTP militants including an Afghan and a commander were killed in a CTD raid in Badaber while two TTP militants were arrested in a raid in Karachi.
On 3 September, three TTP insurgents including TTP governor for Pishin were killed in a UCAV strike in Harnai District, while three more were killed in Bannu District. An insurgent attack on Shadi Khel Police Station in Lakki Marwat District was repulsed by security forces and an off-duty FC soldier was killed by insurgents in Tank District.
On 4 September, a policeman was killed in an insurgent attack in Peshawar, while an SHO was abducted by insurgents in Kurram.
On 5 September, five TTP insurgents were killed in a CTD raid in Bannu while TTP claimed to have killed a CTD personnel in Peshawar. A girl was killed in a quadcopter strike in Kohat District and a government school was destroyed by militants in Tank District. A TTP attack on Darban checkpost in DI Khan district was repulsed by Pakistani forces. Three Afghan security guards were killed and two went missing in Duki District in an attack by TTP. 
On 6 September, 12 TTP insurgents were killed in an operation in North waziristan while two more militants and two Pakistani militiamen were killed in skirmishes in South Waziristan, four more insurgents were killed in an operation in Hangu. A drone strike in Kohat led to the death of one civilian.
On 7 September, six suspected insurgents were captured from Matta in Swat District, four insurgents were killed in Kurram District in the operation leading to the recovery of the abducted SHO and another person, while insurgents blew up a BHU in Tank District.
On 8 September, 27 TTP insurgents attempting to infiltrate the Pak-Afghan border were killed by Pakistani forces in North Waziristan  while four including an Afghan were killed by Pakistani forces in Kurram District.
On 9 September, a policeman was killed and another was injured in an insurgent attack on a patrol near Shatakai dam. A drone strike took place near an oil and gas facility in Karak District while a girl was killed in a TTP quadcopter strike during an operation in Kohat. Four insurgents were killed and three wounded in a foiled attack on the Anar China checkpost in Hangu District while one more was killed in Lakki Marwat District.
On 10 September, six TTP militants were killed in an operation involving quadcopter strikes in North Waziristan.
On 11 September, two police constables were killed by insurgents, one in Lakki Marwat and one in Bannu District.
On 12 September, Pakistan's Federal Government designated 26 districts of KP as "hard districts" and began providing risk allowance to security and administrative personnel worth 250% of their basic pay. Four insurgents were killed in an operation in Bara tehsil.
On 13 September, a wanted TTP militant was killed in a CTD-Rangers joint raid in Karachi.
On 14 September, an Elite Force personnel was killed by insurgents in Bannu District while an insurgent was killed in Khyber District.
On 15 September, four TTP militants were killed during an operation by Police and Lakki Police Aman Committee in the Saggai. An insurgent was killed and three policemen were injured in an attack on Sri Bahlol police post in Mardan. Two Hafiz Gul Bahadur group militants were killed in a Peace Committee ambush in South Waziristan. A civilian was killed and another injured in an attack in Upper Dir District.
On 16 September, Sra Khawra police post in Peshawar was targeted with a bomb blast resulting in two policemen being wounded, while a police SI was killed in Swabi District.
On 17 September, eight insurgents were killed in operations in Kurram and four more in North Waziristan, where two insurgents were also wounded. In Hangu District, six soldiers and four militants were killed during an operation. A soldier was killed in a skirmish with insurgents in Wana, while TTP claimed to have captured an FC soldier deployed at Ghulam Khan border sector of Pak-Afghan border.
On 18 September, Ittahid-ul-Mujahideen Pakistan militants attacked the Old Police Lines complex in Kohat, resulting in 31 deaths and 103 injuries. Pakistan accused Afghanistan of sponsoring terrorism and intensifies counterterrorism operations against Afghanistan. Following this, exchanges of fire took place between Pakistani and Afghan forces in Teri Mangal. Taliban urged Saudi Arabia to mediate between the two countries. Dead bodies of 4 surrendered TTP insurgents were also found in DI Khan.
On 19 September, eight militants were reported to have been killed in retaliatory and clearance operations following the attack in Kohat, the previous day. Two suspected insurgents were killed in two encounters in Karachi. A grenade attack targeting Sheikhan police post in Peshawar failed, while an attack on Sargah Nala post in Gilgit Baltistan was repulsed by Pakistani forces.
On 20 September, six Pakistani soldiers and nine militants were killed in an exchange of fire in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa at Hangu close to the border. Two TTP insurgents were killed and four were injured in a quadcopter strike in Lakki Marwat District. 
On 21 September, Pakistan launched airstrikes on the provinces of Paktika and Kunar in retaliation for the Kohat attack. Kunar's Nurgal district was hit at 4:00 local time, striking a family home and killing three family members and four others. Paktika's Barmal district was hit at 3:00, a shop and an unoccupied house were destroyed in the bombardment. Pakistani authorities denied striking civilians and said the attacks struck militant hideouts perfectly, supposedly killing 28 militants and multiple suicide bombers. These airstrikes also accompanied ground operations by Pakistani forces. ISPR also claimed that 13 TTP militants were killed during an operation in the Shaban area of Quetta District. RFE/RL reported that Pakistan had recruited ex-ANA personnel in paid roles for counter-insurgent operations. Pakistani Defence Minister, Khwaja Asif, alleged that 70-80% of all insurgents in Pakistan were Afghan nationals.
On 22 September, it was reported that several Pakistani Taliban members attempted to cross the border at Kurram from Nangarhar and Paktia in Afghanistan. After being identified by Pakistani troops, they reportedly began firing on Pakistani checkposts. In retaliation, Pakistani troops launched multiple attacks on Afghan checkposts and defensive positions, supposedly causing several to flee. Zazi Aryub district in Paktika also saw skirmishes. A militant commander was killed by SSG in Bannu District, while five insurgents surrendered.
On 23 September, there were supposedly drone strikes inside Pakistan. While Pakistan blamed Afghanistan, Taliban officials denied the use of drones. Eight drones were downed by Pakistani Air defenses near Torkham border while quadcopter strikes targeted Pakistani positions in Kark Kot and Spin Khwara Khula areas of South Waziristan, while TTP released footage of having ambushed a military column near the Pak-Afghan border there as well. Pakistani forces, meanwhile claimed to have conducted operations against Afghan positions in the Kurram Sector. Four TTP militants were also killed in an operation in North Waziristan while a person was killed in a shootout in South Waziristan.
On 24 September, Pakistan carried out airstrikes on 10 sites in Afghanistan. Kandahar, Paktia and Khost were struck and at least four civilians were killed. Afghanistan vowed to respond. The same day, local Afghan sources like Hariyat Media claimed that a Pakistani drone was intercepted over the Garmsir district near a Taliban border brigade position. Pakistan claimed that 13 Afghan Taliban militants were killed in skirmishes over the night of 24 September, a claim which was denied by Afghanistan, Afghan Taliban's 205 Al-Badr Corps claimed to have destroyed a Pakistani post in Spin Boldak. Pakistan denied Afghan claims of its post being destroyed and released footage of strikes on Afghan positions in Gulistan sector of the border. Aral Hathi Khel in Bannu District allegedly came under siege by insurgents using drones and IEDs. A TTP commander was killed in an operation in South Waziristan while two suspected insurgents were killed in an operation in Bannu.
On 25 September, skirmishes took place between Pakistani and Afghan forces in Chaman sector, with the latter trying to infiltrate across the border, the infiltration attempt was foiled and several casualties were inflicted, mortars and drones were also used, at least 14 Afghan Taliban were reported to have been killed in these skirmishes by some reports. Pakistan claimed that TTP had established military training centres in Kunar, Nangarhar, Khost and Paktika with Afghan Taliban joining their ranks. A TTP militant was killed in Bannu District while an FC soldier was killed in a clash in Tirah.
On 26 September, heavy skirmishes were reported along the border in Kurram, Nangarhar and Paktika with gunfire, mortar strikes and artillery strikes being exchanged. A VBIED suicide attack on the Aman Mela police peace committee checkpost in Dera Ismail Khan resulted in the deaths of 12 people and wounding of 35 more, two rescue personnel were further killed as ambulances transporting came under fire by insurgents.
On 27 September, Afghanistan's Defence Ministry claimed that 28 fighters were killed in Nuristan who had crossed the border from Pakistan. The ministry also claimed that most of the fighters were former Afghan government security personnel recruited by ISI. Additionally, claims were made that there were Islamic State fighters among the ranks supported by Pakistani militias. AFF claimed that 37 Taliban had been killed and several wounded in these clashes, moreover they also claimed to have seized territory in Kunar and Nuristan provinces. Clashes between Pakistan and Afghan forces continued into the morning where a woman was killed and a child was injured in a Pakistani mortar strike in Kurram District.
On 28 September, four TTP militants were killed in an operation in DI Khan District. Three traffic policemen were killed by an insurgent attack in Tank District. Two dead insurgents were recovered during an operation in Gulbaz Dehqan area of Lakki Marwat District. Seven security personnel were abducted by insurgents in Kurram District.
On 29 September, Taliban claimed that they had killed 41 Pakistan-backed militants and captured 62, with the fighting in Nuristan coming to an end. A suicide bomber died in a premature detonation in Tank District. 13 TTP insurgents were killed in two different areas in Khyber District of which five were killed in Bara, two more were killed in Chagai, while three more were killed in Mirali, while one was captured from Sahiwal District. Clashes between Taliban and AFF resumed in Nuristan.
On 30 September, an insurgent was killed in an operation in Bara. Afghanistan alleged Pakistani involvement in the clashes in Nuristan, which was later rejected by Pakistan, an official stated that ties with the Taliban had reached a point of no return.
On 1 October, more airstrikes took place. While Pakistan claimed that 22 militants were targeted, Taliban claimed that 9 civilians were killed and 11 others were wounded. Civilian homes in Sheltan district and Garmser district were allegedly targeted. At least three homes were destroyed. Four insurgents were killed in an operation in North Waziristan District. Several insurgent hideouts were destroyed in operations in Karak District, while a joint search and strike operation was started by FC and police in Mohmand District.
On 2 October, seven TTP militants were killed in a military operation in North Waziristan. A policeman was killed and another wounded in an attack in Tank District, another was killed in Peshawar while a peace committee member was killed in South Waziristan. Two drone strikes targeted two Punjab police posts in Taunsa Sharif District. Governor of Kandahar rejected Pakistani claims that a meeting of foreign militants had taken place in the province.
On 3 October, Jhangi and Lakhani Punjab police posts in DG Khan were targeted by TTP using drones, with one personnel being injured. Pakistan claimed to have killed five TTP militants in an operation in South Waziristan while five more were killed in Bajaur.
On 4 October, 15 TTP militants attempting to infiltrate across the Pak-Afghan border in the Ghulam Khan sector were killed by Pakistani forces while eight TTP insurgents were killed in an operation in DI Khan. Three drone strikes on a residential area in South Waziristan led to two civilians being wounded. An insurgent attack on Kangar Bridge Police Checkpost in Bannu District was repelled by Police and local forces, while TTP seized a vehicle from DI Khan.
On 5 October, a Hafiz Gul Bhadur Group TTP militant was killed in a military operation in Tirah while three TTP militants were killed in an operation in DI Khan District. Two insurgents and a peace committee member were killed in a clash in Tank District while two were killed in a police encounter in Bannu District. A child was killed and seven were injured in a quadcopter strike in Mirali. Afghan foreign minister said that the Pak-Afghan disputes can be solved via diplomacy.
On 6 October, five TTP militants were killed and two were injured in a military operation in North Waziristan, three including an Afghan were killed in Tank District while three more were killed in an encounter in Bannu District. Four FBR personnel and one traffic policeman were killed while another traffic policeman was wounded in two separate attacks in DI Khan. A soldier was killed by insurgents in Tirah while a Police post construction site was blown up in Khyber District. Three NGO healthcare workers were abducted from Tank District.
On 7 October, 13 TTP militants were killed in a military operation in North Waziristan. while eight more were killed in Lakki Marwat. An SHO and another policeman were killed in an attack in Tank District while seven policemen were wounded in an insurgent attack targeting the Shadi Pur police post in Kohat District.
On 8 October, nine TTP militants including four commanders were killed in a military operation in North Waziristan. Three policemen went MIA in Nowshehra District A civilian was killed and another injured in an attack in Bajaur District, while insurgents set up blockades in South Waziristan. 
On 9 October, seven TTP militants were killed in a military operation in North Waziristan, three TTP-Bhittani militants were killed in a CTD-Police operation in Tank District while a TTP-HGB commander was killed in South Waziristan. Raghzai police station in South Waziristan was targeted in a drone attack, while another quadcopter strike occurred in Lakki Marwat. A school headmaster was abducted from Orakzai District.
On 10 October, clashes took place between Pakistani forces and Taliban's 203 Mansoori Corps in Dand aw Patan Aryob Zazi districts of Paktia, with the Pakistani side launching 14 ballistic missiles and multiple drones targeting several sites. A wanted TTP militant was killed in a peace committee operation in Bannu District, while the Afghan commander of Shamshad group was killed in an interfactional clash in South Waziristan. Two policemen were killed in two separate attacks in Khyber District, claimed by TTP. A rocket strike hit the FC Farhad Camp in Wana, while insurgents blew up a gas pipeline in Lakki Marwat District.
On 11 October, 2026 Khyber Pakhtunkhwa state of emergency was declared. Pakistani forces foiled an infiltration attempt by militants across the border in Kurram District, with 12 TTP militants and one soldier being killed in the skirmishes, while a weapons smuggling attempt across the border was foiled in Pishin District. A TTP militant was killed in a foiled attack on Bomb Disposal Squad in North Waziristan District, while an alleged Army informant was killed by TTP in DI Khan District. Afghan Talian started to construct tunnels and fortifications in multiple provinces bordering Pakistan.
On 12 October, a policeman was killed in an attack in Nowshera District, while six civilians were wounded in a drone strike in DI Khan District. CTD and FIA captured a TTP insurgent from Karachi.
On 13 October, five insurgents including an IMP commander were killed in two operations in Bannu District, while four TTP militants were killed in an operation in Lakki Marwat District. An IED was neutralized in Karak District by police. A child was injured in skirmishes in South Waziristan.
On 14 October, a police constable was killed and two civilians were wounded in an insurgent attack in Bajaur District. Five TTP militants and a soldier were killed in a military operation and an Army captain was injured in an IED attack in Tank District. A TTP militant was killed and another was injured in Lakki Marwat District.
On 15 October, three civilians were killed and five were injured in a mortar strike in South Waziristan during skirmishes between Pakistani forces and TTP. Four TTP militants were killed in Mirali, three in Bajaur and three more alleged TTP militants were killed in Swat District. An FC soldier was abducted from Hangu District.
On 16 October, six TTP militants were captured during operations in Balochistan while four were killed in a drone strike in Chagai District. Ten insurgents were killed by Police and Orakzai Scouts in Orakzai, four were killed and eight injured in Tirah while an HGB commander was killed in Lakki Marwat. A policeman was killed in an insurgent attack on Spina Mela post in Peshawar, and five policemen were wounded in an attack on Gumbati checkpost in Bannu district while a quadcopter struck Tank City Police Station.
On 17 October, Pakistani and Afghan forces clashed in Kurram-Paktia sector with two FC soldiers being killed in the skirmish, however, Afghan Taliban claimed to have killed 13 Pakistani soldiers and wounding six. Pakistani forces launched artillery strikes into Afghanistan's Paktika province with an Afghan Taliban being killed in the skirmishes. Pakistan also claimed to have destroyed an Afghan Taliban base in Kurram sector, killing several Taliban. Taliban also started moving military equipment to Kandahar and Helmand provinces, bordering Pakistan.
On 18 October, an attack on Bara Police Station in Khyber District left one person injured while four insurgents were captured during an operation in Lakki Marwat District.
On 19 October, heavy skirmishes took place between Pakistani and Afghan forces for hours in Paktia province, meanwhile, six insurgents were killed in an operation in Matani near Peshawar while a civilian was killed in Bajaur District.
On 20 October, five TTP-Geedar Group militants were killed in a drone strike in Bannu District, and an insurgent commander was killed in Lakki Marwat. An SHO was assassinated by militants in Miranshah.
On 21 October, five TTP militants were killed in Kurram District, four in North Waziristan and another in Bannu District, several hideouts were destroyed in Lakki Marwat. A civilian was killed in crossfire between military and insurgents in Dera Ismail Khan District.
On 22 October, four policemen and two insurgents were killed in a clash in Karak District, while three TTP militants including an Afghan were killed in an operation in Mirali. TTP ambushed a military patrol composed of three vehicles in Garyum in North Waziristan, as well as a police patrol near Miryan Police Station in Bannu District with gunfire and a VBIED, the latter resulting in injuries to two civilians.
On 23 October, Police claimed to have completed an operation with 14 insurgents killed in Karak District, while a TTP militant was captured from Karachi. Three children were injured in a quadcopter strike in Bannu District.
On 24 October, six TTP militants and two soldiers were killed in an operation in DI Khan District. A TTP commander was killed in Qila Saifullah District and another in Khyber District. An IED targeted a police vehicle in Bannu while Pakistani and TTP forces skirmished in North Waziristan.
On 25 October, a soldier of 3rd Azad Kashmir Regiment was killed in a sniper attack on a security post in South Waziristan while drone strikes targeted a Police post in Badaber and Bagyari Joint Post of the 101 Wing, Khyber Rifles in Khyber District, the former being neutralized. A civilian was abducted by IMP and an IED was neutralized in Lakki Marwat District. A mortar strike in DI Khan led to the deaths of one child and wounding of three civilians.
On 26 October, three militants were killed in an operation in South Waziristan while an attack on Warmando Mela checkpost in Khyber District and a drone strike on Hassankhel Police Station were foiled by police forces. a civilian was killed in a militant drone strike in Bannu District while four were wounded in drone strikes in South Waziristan. Two IEDs were neutralized in Mirali.
On 27 October, Afghan forces struck Pakistani territory in Angoor Ada killing one civilian and wounding five others, Taliban claimed that the skirmishes were targeted after Pakistani strikes on Afghan territory including four drone strikes targeting the deputy commissioner office and military positions in Paktika as well as stating that multiple Pakistani soldiers had been killed or wounded in these skirmishes. An IED attack in Bannu District left one dead and three injured, while a policeman was killed in Mirali.
On 28 October, Pakistani forces engaged multiple Afghan border posts, mortar positions and defensive bunkers with small and heavy weapons, including artillery, following cross-border firing near Angoor Adda a day earlier. Pakistan also claimed that Afghan Taliban had abandoned multiple posts in the area. Pakistan claimed that its forces had destroyed seven Afghan border posts. Skirmishes also took place at the Torkham border crossing. Five militants were killed in an operation in Bannu District and five in DI Khan.
On 29 October, Pakistani forces destroyed the Shakin base of Afghan Taliban with artillery and airstrikes, the Taliban had withdrew 5 kilometres away but the base was struck as they were attempting to reoccupy it. Skirmishes were also reported along the Pak-Afghan border in South Waziristan. Five TTP-Huzaifa group militants were killed in a CTD operation in Mattani. One civilian was killed in an Army drone strike and two civilians injured in separate drone strike in South Waziristan, a military drone was also shot down. Five militants were killed and 16 injured in Tank District while a TTP militant was killed in Kurram District. Two soldiers were killed in an IMP ambush in South Waziristan while TTP killed an alleged Army collaborator in Bannu District.
On 30 October, skirmishes between Pakistan and Afghan forces continued, an Afghan child was killed and four were injured in a Pakistani mortar explosion in Paktika. Three TTP militants were killed and several injured in a drone strike in South Waziristan and another belonging to TTP's Jaish-e-Umari faction was killed in Mirali. In Bannu, a policeman was killed and another was abducted, a policeman was killed in an insurgent attack on Salai Patri post in Bajaur while a constable was killed in Lakki Marwat District with retaliatory operations leading to the deaths of two TTP militants. An insurgent was killed in Bannu District, while a civilian was killed in an insurgent attack on a mosque in Bajaur District.
On 31 October, a policeman was killed and two people were injured in firing outside a courtroom in Lakki Marwat District. Six drone strikes hit the village of Harmuz in North Waziristan while a civilian was killed in another drone strike in Lakki Marwat. Assistant Commissioner of Mansehra was injured in an attack in Nowshera. Two militants were killed in an operation in Orakzai District, while two policemen were injured during the clash. Four insurgents were killed in Lakki Marwat and four in Mohmand District in security forces operations, while TTP claimed to have killed an alleged Army informant in South Waziristan. 
On 1 November, Pakistani and Afghan forces skirmished in South Waziristan exchanging fire, with Taliban allegedly leaving behind posts. An Afghan civilian was killed and two were injured in Pakistani rocket strikes on Shikin District in Paktika province. Pakistani and Afghan forces also skirmished at Torkham with te Taliban evacuating a deportee camp due to the clashes. A civilian was injured in a VBIED attack on a police van while three policemen were injured in a quadcopter strike on Bakakhel Tower No. 3, both in Bannu District. TTP shot down a military drone in South Waziristan and destroyed a surveillance camera in Tank District.
On 2 November, two Gul Bahadur Group militants were killed in an operation in North Waziristan and two more were killed in Bannu District. a soldier was killed was killed and another wounded in a drone strike on a camp in Lakki Marwat District. Two police personnel in the security detail of a polio vaccination team were killed and one was injured in Mohmand District while four polio vaccination workers were abducted by insurgents from Tank District, with two being released later. A police vehicle was damaged in an IED attack in Bannu District.
On 3 November, two TTP insurgents including a suicide bomber were killed in a police encounter in Lakki Marwat District, while a third was injured, while two more militants were killed in Tank District by locals. Heavy skirmishes and even airstrikes were reported in Panjpai area of Quetta District. Drone strikes on Malazai Police Station and a nearby FC checkpoint in Tank District resulted in three personnel being injured.
On 4 November, four insurgents were killed in an operation in Bajaur District, three TTP militants were killed in Tank District while a preparing suicide bomber was neutralized in Kurram District. Two civilians were injured in a drone strike in South Waziristan while a polio vaccination supervisor was abducted by insurgents from Jamrud. Yaadgar-e-Shuhada Police Checkpost in Dera Ismail Khan District was attacked by insurgents. 
On 5 November, Pakistani and Afghan forces skirmished in the Shaluzan sector of Kurram district, following a TTP infiltration attempt across the border, multiple Afghan posts were damaged in the clashes, an Afghan Taliban was also captured by Pakistani forces in this attempt. an insurgent was killed in a drone strike in Khyber District and another in Bannu District. Four people including a policeman and an FC soldier were abducted by insurgents blockading a road in Lakki Marwat District, while an FC soldier was abducted and later killed in Dera Ismail Khan, a polio vaccination team was also attacked in Mohmand District. A civilian was killed and another injured in two insurgent attacks in North Waziristan. 
On 6 November, dead body of a TTP militant was found dumped in Upper Dir District.
On 7 November, a Bomb Disposal Squad member was killed in an IED Explosion in South Waziristan, while a policeman and his son were killed in an attack in Tank District. Four TTP militants were killed in an operation in Bannu District, TTP Quetta intelligence chief was killed in Panjpai after three days of clashes while a Lashkar al-Zil (AQIS) commander was killed in an operation in South Waziristan. A drone strike hit a residential house in Tank District. 
On 8 November, four TTP militants were killed in an operation in Khyber District and four more were killed in Bajaur District. An FC soldier was killed in a sniper attack in Tank District and a peace committee member was killed in Kohat. Militant infrastructure and hideouts were destroyed in North Waziristan. 
On 9 November, a policeman was killed and three were wounded in an attack by IMP on a police post in Hangu District. Three polio vaccination workers were abducted from Tank District.
On 10 November, Pakistani forces foiled an insurgent infiltration attempt across the Pakistan-Afghanistan border in North Waziristan killing six insurgents while an insurgent died in a premature IED detonation in Tank District.
On 11 November, TTP ambushed police vehicles in Kohat District with the ensuing battle resulting in 10 policemen and 18 insurgents being killed, 12 policemen were injured as well. Two policemen were killed and one injured in an attack on another patrol in Swabi District while a bomb blast targeted the Bandkorai Police Station in Dera Ismail Khan. Four insurgents were killed in a military operation in Bajaur District.
On 13 November, ISPR claimed that Pakistani forces had killed 35 TTP militants in Mir Ali, eight in Orakzai district and 31 militants in Kurram area of Quetta.

== Censorship ==
During the conflict, the Taliban's intelligence agency, the General Directorate of Intelligence (GDI), ordered Afghan domestic media outlets not to cover areas targeted in recent Pakistani airstrikes. In some cases, intelligence personnel monitored media offices and newsroom operations to enforce the directive, and media outlets were warned against defying the order. Taliban intelligence officials also warned residents against publishing images or details of locations in Afghanistan targeted by Pakistani strikes. 
Afghan local sources stated that the Taliban were restricting access to information about their own casualties, as well as those among civilians. They added that only Taliban members were allowed to take images of affected areas and victims, making independent verification of casualties and damage difficult. According to the sources, even Taliban controlled media outlets were not allowed to photograph the sites and areas targeted by Pakistan's airstrikes, and there were no accurate statistics on the casualties of civilians and Taliban fighters. 
On 1 March, the Taliban suspended the broadcasts of Rah-e-Farda radio and television in Kabul, a channel affiliated with Mohammad Mohaqiq. The suspension was linked to remarks by Mohammad Mohaqiq, which reportedly criticized the Taliban's recent retaliatory attacks against Pakistan. On 5 March, the Taliban increased pressure on local media outlets, warning journalists not to report on attacks, particularly those targeting Taliban military sites. Under the new instructions, domestic media organizations were told not to report the locations or number of Pakistani airstrikes. On 17 March, the General Directorate of Intelligence (GDI) warned local media outlets not to report casualties among Taliban forces from Pakistani airstrikes, saying that doing so could have serious consequences. Afghan Media Support Organization (AMSO) reported that the Taliban had imposed extensive restrictions on the media, including censorship of security-related events, and restrictions on reporting Taliban casualties. It said that journalists had been forced to publish pro-Taliban reports, including during the border clashes with Pakistan, and that their online activities were being monitored.

== Analysis ==
Sultan Ahmad Baheen, former Afghan ambassador to China, suggested that the Pakistani attacks coincided with the 2026 Iran war to minimize international attention on the airstrikes. He claimed that "Pakistan does not want a fully stable and independent Afghanistan" in the long term, but rather a political landscape in Kabul that remains dependent on Islamabad.
Sardar Rahimi, an Afghan researcher in international relations at INALCO, viewed the timing of Pakistan's attacks amid the events in Iran as a strategic opportunity. He suggested that Pakistan, economically and militarily vulnerable in its war with the Taliban, needed US support and saw the attack on Bagram airfield as a projection to US president Donald Trump of Pakistan's alignment with US interests. He stated that Pakistan cannot continue the conflict without US support, and therefore, attacked Bagram airfield for political purposes.
Analysts warned that Afghanistan's drone attacks on Pakistan, targeting garrison cities among other important places, signaled a troubling trend. In response, the government imposed a nationwide drone flight ban and briefly restricted airspace over Islamabad. In Pakistan's security discourse, the focus shifted from the extent of damage caused by drones to concerns over their ability to penetrate deep into the country. This raised questions about potential vulnerabilities in Pakistan's defense preparedness. Abdul Basit, senior associate fellow at the International Centre for Political Violence and Terrorism Research (ICPVTR), stressed that the concern was not the drones' sophistication, but their presence in Pakistan's capital. Taliban drones forced airspace closures and targeted deep within the country, escalating the threat both horizontally and vertically. Hammad Waleed, a research associate at Pakistan's Strategic Vision Institute, stated that while Pakistan's air defense could counter numbered drone projectiles, it would struggle against drone swarms.

== Impact ==
According to the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA), the civilian infrastructure in Eastern Afghanistan suffered as a result of hostilities. As of late April 2026, about 19 health facilities were closed, suspended or operating at reduced capacity. About 78,000 people suffered from limited access to healthcare as a consequence. Education services also faced disruptions with more than 13,000 students affected in Kunar and Nangarhar provinces. Water systems were damaged in at least six villages.
Between late February and late April, approximately 100,900 people were displaced across Khost, Kunar, Nangarhar, Nuristan, Paktia, and Paktika provinces. Continuous shelling and unexploded ordnances constrained access for humanitarian operations in some of these provinces. 
Death counts, especially the toll on civilians, remained disputed during the course of the conflict. While the Taliban claimed 800 Afghan civilians were killed by April, Pakistan claimed that its forces killed over 640 militants and 850 'facilitators.' According to Azizullah Aziz, a journalist and eastern zone coordinator of the Afghan Journalists Safety Committee, most of the attacks were carried out "at night, during Ramadan."
According to UN Secretary-General's spokesperson Stéphane Dujarric, more than 1,100 civilian casualties were documented in Afghanistan resulting from cross-Durand Line violence by October 2026.
Amid the conflict, the deportation of Afghans from Pakistan continued. According to the International Organization for Migration (IOM) in Kandahar, while the deportations through the Torkham crossing paused in March, repatriations continued through the Spin Boldak crossing.

== Reactions ==

=== Domestic ===
 Afghanistan: Afghanistan's Ministry of Defence condemned the airstrikes, claiming that Pakistan had "hit a religious school and residential homes". Foreign Minister Amir Khan Muttaqi said Afghanistan was "facing an imposed war" from Pakistan. Taliban spokesman, Zabihullah Mujahid, said Afghanistan had not initiated the conflict with Pakistan and that its forces were acting only in self-defence. He also stated that Taliban forces were not violating Pakistani territory and were responding only to protect the population.
 Afghanistan Freedom Front: The Afghan Freedom Front said the Taliban had moved Pakistani Taliban militants into government buildings and crowded civilian areas, accusing them of using civilians as human shields. The Front also criticized the Taliban for secrecy and propaganda amid Pakistani attacks, condemned civilian killings, called for an independent international investigation, and urged Afghans not to be misled by Taliban messaging.
 National Resistance Front: Ahmad Massoud said Pakistan's strikes were a consequence of Taliban policies, accusing the group of sheltering the Pakistani Taliban, Al-Qaeda, and other militant organisations and turning Afghanistan into a centre of regional insecurity. At the same time, he rejected foreign military attacks and political deals with the Taliban, arguing that Afghanistan's freedom and any lasting solution must come from the Afghan people themselves through a coordinated and legitimate national effort. Fazel Ahmed Manawi, a senior NRF leader praised Pakistan for its air operations and voiced support.
 Afghan United Front: Sami Sadat, a former Afghan army commander, described the agreement between tribal elders from eastern Afghanistan and Pakistan's Chitral region as a humiliation, saying that Afghans had been reduced to seeking security for their villages and districts from the Pakistani military. He called the situation a historic disgrace brought about by the Taliban.
 Pakistan: Pakistan's Minister of Defence Khawaja Asif declared an "open war" between the two countries.

=== International ===

==== Nations ====
 India: Randhir Jaiswal, the official spokesperson of the Ministry of External Affairs, expressed strong condemnation of the strikes and expressed support for Afghanistan's sovereignty and territorial integrity.
 Qatar: Qatari foreign minister Mohammed bin Abdulaziz Al Khulaifi discussed with Pakistani Foreign Minister Muhammad Ishaq Dar ways to reduce tension between Pakistan and Afghanistan, thereby strengthening security and stability in the region.
 Russia: The Russian government offered to mediate the situation and urged both nations to halt cross-border attacks.
 Saudi Arabia: Prince Faisal bin Farhan and officials in the Pakistani government discussed ways to reduce regional tensions during a phone call.
 United States: The White House stated that it will continue to monitor the situation closely and expressed support for Pakistan against the Taliban attacks. US president Donald Trump praised both Shehbaz Sharif and Asim Munir for fighting against Taliban forces.
In addition, Bangladesh, China, Egypt, Iran, Iraq, Jordan, Malaysia, and Uzbekistan also called for a ceasefire to end hostilities and promoted dialogue to resolve border tensions.

==== Supranational ====
 United Nations: UN Assistance Mission in Afghanistan (UNAMA) urged both nations to cease hostilities and to take steps to prevent harm to civilians. Richard Bennett, the UN Special Rapporteur on the situation of human rights in Afghanistan, expressed concern over airstrikes in Nangarhar and Paktika, calling on the belligerent parties to exercise "maximum restraint". He stated deep concern for "a significant number of children and civilians" who were killed following the hostilities. Bennett, while calling for accountability over civilian deaths resulting from the conflict, also called on International Criminal Court to consider investigating the alleged attacks across the Durand Line and stated that Pakistani airstrikes that killed Afghan civilians may constitute war crimes.
 European Union: In a brief statement, the EU Council called on all actors for immediate de-escalation and a halt of hostilities in the area. It reiterated to the Taliban that Afghan territory must not be used to threaten or attack other countries and calls on them to take effective action against all terrorist groups operating in or from Afghanistan.

The 2026 Varsity Cup was the 19th season of the Varsity Cup, the premier competition in the annual Varsity Rugby series in South Africa for men's rugby union. The tournament took place between eight university teams and played between 16 February and 13 April 2026. UP Tuks were crowned champions, securing a record sixth Varsity Cup title, the most by any team in the competition's history.
This competition forms part of the broader Varsity Rugby programme administered by Varsity Sport, which aims to promote university rugby and provide a pathway for emerging talent into professional rugby structures. Matches were broadcast nationally on SuperSport.
The UCT Ikey Tigers entered the 2026 season as the former winners of the Varsity Cup Trophy after beating Maties in the 2025 final. The 2026 edition was staged under the campaign theme "Who's NXT?", highlighting Varsity Cup's role as a launchpad for future professional and international players and introducing the new Tap-or-Kick post-try power play law to further encourage attacking rugby. Matches were broadcast nationally on SuperSport.

== Competition rules and information ==
Eight university teams participated in the 2026 Varsity Cup. During the pool stage, each team played the other seven sides once, either home or away.
Teams were awarded:

four points for a win
two points for a draw
one bonus point for scoring four or more tries in a match
one bonus point for losing by seven points or fewer
Teams were ranked primarily by log points, and then by points difference (points scored minus points conceded).
The top four teams at the conclusion of the pool stage advanced to the semi-finals. The two highest-ranked teams hosted the semi-finals, and the highest-ranked remaining finalist hosted the final.

title: Gongshuilong
text:
Gongshuilong  (lit. 'Gong River dragon') is an extinct genus of saurolophine hadrosaurid dinosaur known from the Late Cretaceous (Maastrichtian age) Lianhe Formation of China. The genus contains a single species, Gongshuilong fanwei, known from a bonebed representing the disarticulated remains of at least two individuals. Gongshuilong is a member of the group Brachylophosaurini within the Hadrosauridae, and it is the second member of this otherwise North American clade, following Wulagasaurus, found in Asia. It is also the first hadrosaurid to be named from fossils found in South China. Gongshuilong is characterized by the uniquely elongated and curved neural spines of the vertebrae at the end of the tail, forming a tall, sail-like structure.

== Discovery and naming ==
In March 2021, construction was underway for the  East China International Trade and Industrial Zone in the town of Shahe in Ganzhou city, Jiangxi Province, China. During this construction, a bonebed of hadrosaurid dinosaur fossils was exposed in outcrops representing the Late Cretaceous Lianhe Formation. The following month, a permit was obtained from the province's General Office of the Ministry of Natural Resources, allowing researchers from the Basic Geological Survey Institute of the Jiangxi Geological Survey and Exploration Institute (BGS-JX) and Jiangxi Geological Museum (JXGM) to excavate the fossils in two blocks. They were subsequently transferred to the BGS-JX, where they were prepared for research and are now accessioned under the specimen number BGS-JX F001. At least two individuals are represented in the collected material, as indicated by the discovery of two left dentaries (lower jaw bones), scapulae (part of the pectoral girdle), and tibiae (lower leg bones) of slightly different sizes.
In 2026, Han Yao and colleagues described Gongshuilong fanwei as a new genus and species of brachylophosaurin hadrosaurid based on these fossil remains. They established BGS-JX F001-1, a right dentary, as the holotype specimen, and BGS-JX F001-2, a small region of the skull including the left jugal and quadrate bones, as a paratype. The remaining material from the bonebed was additionally referred to this species, and includes more skull bones (maxilla, nasal, and postorbital), mandibular elements (surangulars), four cervical (neck) vertebrae, a partial posterior (rear) dorsal (trunk) vertebra, ten articulated posterior caudal (tail) vertebrae, forelimb (humeri) and pectoral girdle (scapulae and coracoid) elements, and hindlimb (tibia and femur) bones.
The generic name, Gongshuilong , combines the Mandarin Chinese pinyin terms 'Gongshui', for the Gong River near the type locality, with 'long', meaning 'dragon'. The specific name, fanwei, is another pinyin term alluding the prominent sail-like tail morphology that characterizes this species. While hadrosaurid bones have previously been identified in the Ganzhou region in South China, including a fragmentary skeleton and eggs bearing embryos, Gongshuilong is the first member of this clade found in South China to receive a scientific name.

== Description ==

Gongshuilong is recognized as a medium-sized member of the hadrosaurid clade Saurolophinae, with an estimated adult body length of 7 metres (23 ft). The neural spines of the posterior caudal vertebrae are greatly elongate, at 8.5 times as tall as the centrum they are attached to, and somewhat recurved. This gives the end of the tail a tall, sail-like structure. This particular anatomical feature is unique to Gongshuilong, and has not been recognized in other members of the larger clade Iguanodontia.

== Classification ==
To test the affinities and relationships of Gongshuilong, Yao and colleagues included it in an updated version of the phylogenetic matrix of Dai et al. (2025). They recovered Gongshuilong as a member of the tribe Brachylophosaurini within the hadrosaurid clade Saurolophinae. The analysis found an unresolved polytomy within this clade, comprising Gongshuilong, Wulagasaurus, Acristavus, and a clade comprising Maiasaura, Brachylophosaurus, and Probrachylophosaurus. Wulagasaurus is the only other Chinese brachylophosaurin, while the remaining taxa are known from North America. The results of this analysis are displayed in the cladogram below:

These will include tiered open-age competitions across metropolitan and regional New South Wales, as well as a suite of age-based pathway competitions for both male and female players. Along with the Queensland Rugby League, these competitions form a key part of the pathway into the National Rugby League (NRL) and NRLW.

== Jersey Flegg Cup ==

title: 2026 United Bowl
text:
The 2026 United Bowl was the third championship of the United Football League, and it was the first to be played under the United Bowl name. The game was played on June 13, 2026, at Audi Field in Washington, D.C.. The contest determined the champion of the 2026 UFL season and was played between the Louisville Kings and the DC Defenders. The game began at 3:00 p.m. EDT and aired on ABC. The Kings won 27–20, earning their first United Bowl title.

== Background ==

=== Host selection ===
Audi Field had previously been the first choice to host the 2025 championship but was unable to do so because of schedule conflicts with the 2025 FIFA Club World Cup. 

=== UFL playoffs ===

==== Bracket ====

== Teams ==

=== DC Defenders ===

The DC Defenders finished the 2026 season with a 5–5 record. They made their second appearance in the UFL championship game after winning the title in 2025 by defeating the Michigan Panthers, 58–34. DC also played in the 2023 XFL Championship Game, a loss to the Arlington Renegades.

=== Louisville Kings ===

The Louisville Kings finished their first season in existence with a 6–4 record, having rebounded from an 0–3 start to win six of their last seven games. The turnaround was in part caused by the trading of their original starting quarterback Jason Bean to DC; Bean then rose to the Defenders' starting quarterback position after an injury to longtime Defenders starter Jordan Ta'amu.

== Matchup ==
The matchup marked the third meeting between the two teams during the season, with Louisville winning the previous two contests. DC made its third championship game appearance in franchise history and its second in the UFL. Although the game was originally designated as a neutral-site championship, it was held at the home stadium of the Defenders. The Defenders entered the game without 2025 UFL championship game MVP quarterback Jordan Ta'amu, who suffered a torn ACL during a Week 8 loss to the Kings. Following an ineffective performance by backup quarterback Spencer Sanders against Orlando, DC turned to third-string quarterback Jason Bean for its Week 10 matchup against the Storm, a game the Defenders lost. Bean, however, later led DC to an upset playoff victory over top-seeded Orlando after the Storm had defeated the Defenders in each of their previous two meetings. Bean began the season as Louisville's starting quarterback, starting the first four games before being traded to DC in exchange for Mike DiLiello. The move opened the door for Chandler Rogers, who went 5–1 as Louisville's starter during the regular season before leading the Kings to a playoff victory over the St. Louis Battlehawks. The championship game also marked the first on-field meeting between Bean and Rogers, who were teammates at Lake Ridge High School in Mansfield, Texas.

== Game summary ==

=== First half ===
Following punts on both opening possessions, scoring opened with a Matt McCrane 48-yard field goal for DC. After Louisville's second consecutive punt, DC running back Xazavian Valladay broke free for a 54-yard run before being chased down and tackled by Keaton Ellis, who forced a fumble that bounced 35 yards into the end zone where Cameron Dantzler recovered for a Louisville touchback.
Early in the second quarter, Rogers was intercepted by Kai Gray. On DC's ensuing possession, a completion from Bean to Ty Scott was forced loose by Corey Mayfield, and the fumble was recovered and returned 12 yards for a Louisville touchdown by Eric Garror, giving the Kings a 7–3 lead. Valladay later redeemed himself on DC's next drive, scoring on a 51-yard touchdown run to regain the lead. Following a Louisville punt, McCrane added a 57-yard field goal for DC. On Louisville's next possession, Rogers was intercepted again by Gray, setting up a 28-yard McCrane field goal that extended DC's lead to 16–7 at halftime.  Despite both quarterbacks being held to fewer than 50 passing yards, the Defenders outgained the Kings 227–62 and held a 209–41 advantage on the ground, while both teams committed two turnovers. Artist 50 Cent performed the halftime show.

=== Second half ===
Louisville scored its first offensive points of the contest on its opening drive with a Tanner Brown 57-yard field goal, set up by a 19-yard run from James Robinson. On DC's ensuing possession, Bean suffered a left shoulder separation on an incomplete third-down pass attempt, ruling him out for the remainder of the game. Brown later cut the deficit to three points with his second field goal of the game, a 38-yard kick. DC then turned to quarterback E. J. Perry, who had been signed on May 25 and had not appeared in the Week 10 game or playoffs to that point. Following a DC three-and-out, Louisville running back Ian Wheeler broke free for a 44-yard go-ahead touchdown run on the first play of the fourth quarter, his eighth touchdown of the season.
After generating just six offensive yards in the third quarter, DC's ensuing drive was derailed when Perry's long completion to Cornell Powell was negated by offensive pass interference. On the same drive, Perry was shortly afterwards intercepted on a deep post route by Dantzler, who returned it 47 yards to the DC 25-yard line. Two plays later, Robinson broke multiple tackles on a 16-yard touchdown run, extending Louisville's lead to 27–16 with just over 12 minutes remaining. A strong kickoff return by Valladay to midfield sparked a promising drive, but multiple penalties stalled the possession. McCrane salvaged the drive with a 60-yard four-point field goal, his fourth of the season, cutting the deficit to 27–20 with just over nine minutes remaining. Following a Louisville three-and-out, Perry led DC inside the red zone. On fourth down from inside the Kings’ 10-yard line, his pass sailed over Powell and fell incomplete with under two minutes remaining. With no timeouts remaining, DC was unable to stop the clock, and Louisville ran out the clock to secure a 27–20 victory and the championship. The Kings finished the season winning eight of their final nine games.
Running back Ian Wheeler was named the game's most valuable player, rushing for 81 yards on 10 carries, including the go-ahead 44-yard touchdown run in the fourth quarter. He also returned a kickoff for 28 yards.

title: 2026 Milan–San Remo
text:
The 2026 Milan–San Remo was a road cycling one-day race that took place on 21 March in north-western Italy. It was the 117th edition of the Milan–San Remo cycling classic.

The race was won by Tadej Pogačar of UAE Team Emirates XRG in a sprint finish against of Tom Pidcock of Pinarello–Q36.5 Pro Cycling Team, after Pogačar attacked on the Cipressa climb for the second year in succession. Third place went to Wout van Aert of Visma–Lease a Bike, the best of the chasing peloton behind.
Pogačar's win was his fourth different Monument victory and was his first victory in the race after four consecutive top-five finishes. The victory marked Pogačar's eleventh in a Monument, tying Roger De Vlaeminck's tally for the second-most Monument wins.

== Teams ==
All eighteen UCI WorldTeams and seven UCI ProTeams participated in the race.
UCI WorldTeams

UCI ProTeams

== Race ==
The route of the 117th edition of Milan–San Remo was similar to recent years edition, with a start in Pavia, just outside Milan. The route leading to San Remo remained largely intact, featuring iconic landmarks such as the Passo del Turchino, the three Capi, the Cipressa, and the pivotal Poggio. The overall race distance was 298 kilometres (185 mi).
Like most recent editions, the race came to life on the lead-up to the penultimate climb of Cipressa. With 32.5 km (20.2 mi) left, a crash brought down several riders, including Tadej Pogačar (UAE Team Emirates XRG) and Wout van Aert (Visma–Lease a Bike) while the reigning winner, Mathieu van der Poel (Alpecin–Premier Tech), was also involved. Pogačar made it back to the peloton at the foot of the Cipressa before being brought to the front by his teammate Brandon McNulty, who began to set a furious pace.
Following a leadout by teammate Isaac Del Toro, Pogačar made his move with 24 km (15 mi) to go and 2.5 km (1.6 mi) from the top of the Cipressa, bringing Tom Pidcock (Pinarello–Q36.5 Pro Cycling Team) and van der Poel with him. The trio worked together to keep the peloton at bay before reaching the foot of the Poggio with an advantage of 10 seconds. On the climb, Pogačar successfully dropped van der Poel with his first attack. He attacked a few more times to shake off Pidcock but to no avail, with the duo reaching the top of the Poggio with a lead of around 20 seconds.
On the Via Roma, Pogačar started his sprint with 200 m (660 ft) left, managing to hold off Pidcock by half a wheel to win the race. Just four seconds behind them, van Aert, who attacked the peloton at the bottom of the Poggio descent, barely held off the peloton to take third place.
Interviewed after the race, Pogačar stated that he thought the crash meant that his chance of victory "was all over". Pogačar complimented Pidcock, stating he is "punchy [and] a really fast guy", noting that he was "a bit afraid when [Pidcock] let me go first" in the final sprint. Pidcock stated that "winning by such close margins, [but] also losing by such close margins, is what makes the times when you win better".
Following the race, UAE Team Emirates XRG mechanics revealed that Pogačar had won the race on a bike with a cracked frame and a rubbing brake, following his crash earlier in the race.

title: Dongoconodon
text:
Dongoconodon (lit. 'Dong's cone tooth') is an extinct genus of early mammal in the order Eutriconodonta known from the Early Cretaceous (Barremian–Aptian age) Jiufotang Formation of China. The genus contains a single species, Dongoconodon platycauda, known from a nearly complete skeleton missing part of the left forelimb. Dongoconodon has a unique pattern of replacement teeth (polyphydonty) compared to most mammals. Several anatomical features, such as evidence for webbed hands and a flattened tail, indicate it had a semiaquatic ecology.

== Discovery and naming ==

The Dongoconodon fossil material was collected by Junyou Wang in 2016 from outcrops of the Jiufotang Formation (Changzigou locality) near Sanjiazi Town in Lingyuan city, Liaoning Province, China. The specimen is housed in the  Inner Mongolia Museum of Natural History, where it is permanently accessioned as specimen IMMNH-PV01700. It consists of a nearly complete, articulated skeleton including the skull, preserved on a single slab. The only missing elements are the left humerus, ulna and radius, three bones of the forelimb.
In 2026, Shundong Bi and colleagues described Dongoconodon platycauda as a new genus and species of eutriconodont based on these fossil remains, designating IMMNH-PV01700 as the holotype specimen. The generic name, Dongoconodon, honors Chinese scientist Junshe Dong and his contributions to vertebrate paleontology research. This is combined with the common eutriconodont suffix '-conodon' (lit. 'cone tooth'), from the Greek κῶνος (kônos) and ὀδών (odṓn). The specific name, platycauda, combines the Greek πλατύς (plătŭ́s), meaning 'flat', with the Latin cauda, meaning tail, referencing the distinctive tail morphology.

== Description and palaeobiology ==

The D. platycauda holotype represents an individual with an estimated body mass of 115–190 grams (0.254–0.419 lb). The skull is flattened but generally triangular in shape and broadest toward the back. The mandible is robust. The jaw shape and caniniform incisors are reminiscent of the related gobiconodontids, suggesting a carnivorous diet involving the active catching and ripping of prey items. The tooth replacement pattern of Dongoconodon is unusual, with multiple generations of teeth indicative of polyphyodonty (continuous replacement of teeth). This contrasts with nearly all other mammals, which are diphyodont (two sets of teeth), and is instead similar to the pattern in many reptiles.
Dongoconodon further exhibits a suite of unique adaptations to a semiaquatic ecology, consistent with features seen in extant semiaquatic mammals. The hands and feet are long and broadened in relation to the limbs, as in the platypus. The arrangement and structure of the phalanges, meta/carpals, and meta/tarsals indicate the digits could be spread, increasing surface area and improving the stroke for swimming. The manual (hand) phalanges bear flanges on the dorsal surfaces, similar to the platypus, marking the attachment points for webbing between the digits. The proximal caudal (tail) vertebrae are broad and flattened, while the vertebrae toward the tip of the tail were longer and more round. This structure is most similar to the extant nutria, where part of the tail is flattened, but the rest is long and tapered.

== Classification ==

Bi et al. (2026) included Dongocondon in a phylogenetic matrix to test its affinities and relationships. It was recovered as the sister taxon to a clade including Spinolestes, Gobiconodon, and Repenomamus, which together comprise the family Gobiconodontidae. These taxa, along with several others, form the early-diverging mammal clade Eutriconodonta. These results are displayed in the cladogram below:

title: Houthi blockade of Saudi Arabia
text:
Starting 20 July 2026, the Houthis of Yemen claimed to impose a maritime and aerial embargo against Saudi Arabia. It marked a major escalation between the Iran-aligned Houthis and the Saudi-led coalition, ending a roughly four-year period of relative calm that had held since a 2022 UN-brokered truce in the Yemeni civil war.

== Background ==

Since the rapid Houthi takeover of Yemen in 2014, Yemen has been divided between the Houthi-controlled north and territory held by the internationally recognized, Saudi-backed government of Yemen (PLC). A 2022 UN-brokered truce substantially reduced large-scale fighting, though Saudi Arabia continued restricting access to Houthi-held ports and Sanaa International Airport, a policy the Houthis have long described as a blockade of Houthi.
Regional tensions rose sharply in 2026 amid the wider conflict between the United States, Israel, and Iran. Following the assassination of Iran's Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei on 28 February 2026 at the outset of the US–Israeli war on Iran, a Houthi delegation travelled to Tehran for his funeral aboard an Iranian aircraft. When the aircraft attempted to return the delegation to Sanaa, Saudi Arabia struck the runway at Sanaa International Airport on 13 July 2026 to prevent the landing, acting at the request of the IRG; the aircraft was diverted instead to the Houthi-controlled Red Sea port city of Hodeidah.
In response, the Houthis launched missiles and drones at Abha International Airport in southern Saudi Arabia the same day. Houthi officials said the group considered itself entitled to strike Saudi airports and impose a "siege" on the kingdom, equating this with restrictions Saudi Arabia had long imposed on the Houthis.

== Declaration of the blockade ==
On 20 July 2026, Yahya Saree, Houthi military spokesman, announced in a televised statement that the Houthis were imposing a maritime embargo on Saudi Arabia, describing the move as based on the principle of "an eye for an eye." Officials did not initially specify which vessels would be targeted, though they indicated that ships calling at Saudi ports or carrying Saudi oil could be at risk. The group also warned that any Saudi military response would be met with a "comprehensive and decisive" escalation and called on supporters to mobilize for a wider confrontation.
Houthi leader Abdul-Malik al-Houthi had earlier threatened Saudi oil facilities directly following the Abha airport strike.

== Strategic and economic context ==

The blockade threatened shipping through the Bab-el-Mandeb Strait, linking the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden, which had become an increasingly important export route for Saudi Arabia. Saudi Arabia had been routing a growing share of its oil exports, reportedly around 70 percent, through Red Sea ports such as Yanbu, partly as an alternative to the Strait of Hormuz, which Iran had closed amid its conflict with the United States. Analysts estimated that a full closure of Bab-el-Mandeb could remove as much as 7 percent of global oil supply from the market, compounding disruptions from reduced flows through Hormuz.
The Houthis had previously conducted an extended campaign against Red Sea shipping beginning in late 2023, during which they reportedly reached informal understandings allowing Russian and Chinese vessels safe passage; the Atlantic Council noted that comparable arrangements might not extend to vessels carrying Saudi oil to Chinese markets.

== Reactions ==

=== Saudi Arabia ===
Saudi Arabia's Foreign Ministry condemned the Houthi announcement, rejected characterizations of its restrictions on Houthi-held territory as a "siege," and stated it would take necessary measures to protect shipping.

=== International ===
The UN Security Council held an emergency session to discuss the escalation, with members expressing concern about the risk of wider regional conflict. Shipping insurers raised premiums for vessels transiting the Red Sea following the announcement.
On 28 July 2026, Reuters reported that China had held direct talks with the Houthis and Iran to enable its tankers to pass through the Red Sea without being attacked. It reported that China was clearing each vessel with the Houthis individually, and both sides have informed Iran of their actions.
